utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine: "... shall be responsible for the overall work of moral guidance within the frameworks of the Croatian Defence Department and in preparing the country for defence. To that end, he shall have under him the following organisational units:" And it goes on to say, number 1, Information and Propaganda Administration, Military, Psychology and Personnel Needs Administration, and, 3, History, Education, and Publishing Administration. I'm now going to ask you to tell me, in September 1992, roughly when you came to the department, who was the assistant head for moral guidance?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: It was Mr. Bozo Rajic at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And who was the head of the Information and Propaganda Department?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That was me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who was the head of the other administration?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: The Military Psychology and Personnel Needs Administration was Mrs. Vera Cubela. She was the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And under 3, the History, Education, and Publishing Administration, who was there?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Mr. Jure Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, Jure Pasalic. Thank you. Now, Mr. Vegar, if I understood you correctly, after the 31st of January, you were still doing the job oft his first administration, that is to say, the Information and Propaganda Administration?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at the following document 2D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm looking at paragraph 6, and I see that he talks about ethical conduct in the units, which is an extremely important issue. Now, the ethical conduct, under whose responsibility was it? I mean, we talk about it, but we don't know who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I understand it, Your Honour, as far as I understand it, Your Honour, as far as I understand this paragraph, I think that everybody was responsible in the army for moral guidance or moral instruction. And in this case the most responsible was the assistant head, which meant Mr. Rajic at that time or I, myself, several months later.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour, for that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, as this was called -- this whole sector was called the Sector for Moral Guidance, does that imply, Mr. Vegar, that all three administrations within the sector were in charge of moral guidance?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, every administration had to contribute to boosting morale and raising the cultural level and general educational level.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now let's look at 2D 00567, the next document. Mr. Vegar, this is a decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department, dated the 17th of October, 1992, and at the time you were in this Sector for Moral Guidance, and it is signed by Mr. Mate Boban -- or, rather, Bruno Stojic and Mr. Mate Boban -- in agreement with Mr. Mate Boban, as it says on the last page. But let's look at D, the Sector for Moral Guidance, and can you tell us -- well, it says the Moral guidance sector, and then it lists the three administrations and the heads of those three administrations, and then it goes on to say that they are appointed by the head of the Defence Department at the proposal from the assistant head for moral guidance. And now take a look at the second paragraph, which says assistant commanders for moral guidance, the operative zone of Southeastern Herzegovina, the operative zone of North-West Herzegovina, and then it lists all the operative zones, in actual fact, so that I don't have to read them all out. It says: "Bruno Pusic, the assistant heads for moral guidance of special purpose units, as well as assistant commander for moral guidance attached to the brigades are appointed by the head of the Defence Department, based on a proposal by the assistant head for moral guidance." Now, can you tell the Trial Chamber what the procedure was actually like, and whether before the establishment of the Defence Department, did any units exist before that of the HVO, and whether in practice this was acted upon, as is stated here?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Before the organisation of the Defence Department, there were a number of Croatian HVO units, and certain persons were appointed to them who were later to work in the IPD sector. Now, unfortunately I have to say here that in practice, all these prerequisites were not respected; that is to say, that the proposal came from the assistant, that is to say, I, myself, and that the procedure, well, it wasn't fully respected. Procedure wasn't fully respected, because as far as I can remember, I did not proposal assistants for IPD.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you remember in what way the assistants for IPD in all the units were put forward? Now, Mr. Vegar, I have the impression that you use the word "sector" when you use IPD assistants in units, you refer to the sectors. Do you differentiate between sectors and assistant for IPD in units?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, we can differentiate between them if, under "sector" we mean just three administrations within the Defence Department, but if we mean everybody in the operative zones, brigades, right down to the battalions, then I think that they also comprise that sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, could you explain that to me? How does that work, in what way?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Well, in the professional sense, you mean? So if we look at the vertical chain, they have to have a chain from top to bottom, and companies, battalions, brigades, operative zones, down to the sector for moral guidance.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're talking about information and the dissemination of information; right?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, sending out information, training, instruction, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me, please, I asked you this question earlier on, did you or do you know in what way assistants for IPDs in units were proposed? Who put their names forward, who agreed, who appointed them, and so on, assistant IPDs in the units that were established after the establishment of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Well, the practice was as follows: The commanders would propose their assistants, and agreement to that was given by the Main Staff. They would have to okay it, authorise it. And their appointment would be made by the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like now like to ask you, Mr. Vegar, to take a look at document 2D 2012, and this is a salary list for November 1992, and you signed it for Mr. Rajic. And here we have six individuals as being employed in the IPD sector, as it says. So this is the payroll list. Now, are these the people you referred to earlier on?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, but we have Natasa Ostojic, who was the secretary, but the others are all people that I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is November 1992. What happened until November 1993? Was there any change in the number of people, or some people left and other came in?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: There were changes, as I explained, earlier. Mr. Bozo Rajic left the sector; Natasa as well, the secretary. Another person became secretary, and also had a private who provided security.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A private who provided security, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. He was -- he provided security, but also escorted journalists and assisted them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we take a look at 2D 685, please. It is a schematic of the moral guidance sector. Could you please explain to the Chamber -- and it is a schematic in the 2D 567, in the decision on the organisation of the Defence Department, and schematics are appendices to that decision. Could you explain what this schematic denotes?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: This is the moral guidance sector's breakdown. There were three administrations: Information Administration; Military, Psychology and Personnel Needs Administration; and History, Culture, Publishing, Sports, et cetera, Administration. And we see here that operations zones, there are commanders who have their assistants for those areas linked with the three administrations within the sector. All brigades within the operations zones have their own assistant commanders for those issues, all battalions, and independent companies had only one person in charge of that, and this entails all four operations zones. Some independent units also had their IPD personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You explained what was the link between the assistants for IPD at units with you. Can we say precisely that this relationship was -- or boiled down to you receiving from them information concerning moral guidance and that you maintained contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: My contacts with them was professional, in terms of providing them assistance, in educating them, training them to perform their basic tasks of the sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say your connections, but would it be the connection of the head of other administrations?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Our idea was for all administration heads to have direct contacts with their respective colleagues at the lower levels. So if head of Administration for Military Psychology would maintain links with assistant commander for Psychological -- Military Psychology at operations zone level, brigade zone level, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Those assistant commanders at companies, battalions, brigades, and operations zones, who were they subordinated to? What was the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: To their corps commanders, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at 2D 1446, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask a question. I'm looking at this scheme, and I'm wondering the following, and maybe you can answer this question about the IPD. There is the issue of propaganda, looking at this chart, you know, related to a given issue within an operating zone, whichever it was, if an event occurred there and that triggered an action to be undertaken. Now, were you in contact with the person who was in charge of the operating area or with the assistant commander to this area to say, for instance, and let me just give you a theoretical example, that UNPROFOR in the region said this or that, that it was false, and that a press release must be released immediately in order to contradict what was said? Now, was that the way in which you operated or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I could and I did contact IPD assistant, and of course such person would be in connection with their commander and would be in a position to provide objective information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. But did you trigger the event, politically speaking? Are you the person who was in charge of communicating this, saying to the commander in the operating area, Well, you need to focus on this or that event, versus another event? Were you actually steering propaganda and training -- or information, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not order any command -- brigade commander or operational zone commander. I could ask assistants for IPD to do something. Information would reach me through such persons of their own initiative and sometimes I sought information and commanders would -- IPD assistants would inform their commanders of everything that they thought was interesting, and this is the chain that ended up with the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, could you please take a look at the following document, 2D [as interpreted], and it's a further explanation of what Judge Antonetti asked you, so it's 2D 446 -- 2D 1446. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic. There is an appointment here into the Command of the 1st Herzegovinian Brigade of persons that Mr. Stojic was authorised to appoint. It starts with "deputy commander." Please take a look at items 22, 23, 24, 25. Could you please explain who those persons were and what posts they occupied?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Assistant commander for IPD under 23, Mr. Nikola Raguz, personal rank was captain.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you please explain the position and whether these were the tasks that you explained?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, those were the tasks that we discussed, and this document appoints him as assistant commander for IPD.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under 24?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: The same, but he's a referent for IPD. It's a lower-level position.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What about 25?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: The 25 is psychology.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have an interesting situation that in the Command of the 1st Herzegovinian Brigade we have a psychologist here. Could you please tell the Chamber whether there were more psychologists in units and what was the situation with the professionals who were supposed to work with HVO HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: We were short of psychologists. We only had four. We needed many, many more. There were psychologists in that area, but many left the area, went abroad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, you explained how the selection and appointment was done, at whose initiative, with the agreement of who, and who did the appointments. I think it's very important. Please, those persons appointed as assistant commanders for IPD, who were they subordinated and responsible to?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: To their commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's take a look at two documents depicting the procedure for appointment. 2D 01450, please take a look at it. This is a proposal of the Rama Brigade of the operation zone, sent to the head of the Defence Department, and we have here listed all the positions that had to be filled in that brigade. Could you please take a look at the last page. Is this the assistant that you referred to, that there was a proposal and that the Main Staff would okay such proposals? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please take a look at the person under the ordinal number of 18. That person is going to be interesting for us. It is a person supposed to perform IPD activities?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, assistant commander for IPD.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the name is?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Marko Dragic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you know that he was appointed, in fact?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then P 02945, the next document. Please take a look at item 18 or -- this is also an appointment signed by Mr. Stojic on the 25th of June, on the basis of a prior proposal. Was that person under 18 appointed?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you discussed, and you were asked by Judge Trechsel about that, you explained how information was collated and compiled for your press conferences that you would then disseminate. Let's see 2D 1353. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a Main Staff document dated the 21st of September, 1992; isn't that so? It's a report by the Main Staff a?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a period where you started working at the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The last page, item 7, the last item in the document --

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As far as information dissemination is concerned that disseminated in the public, the Main Staff would forward reports of the subordinated commands to the IPD department so that it can prepare information for the public. Mr. Vegar, would -- information that you issued would follow this path, as it's stated here?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive information from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And prepared such information to be disseminated to the public?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, please, 2D 687. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is another document by the Main Staff, an order 24th of November 1992 is the date, and that order states that in the past period from the beginning of the war, there were individuals from HVO that issued statements to the media whereby they revealed military secrets or in some other way diminished the reputation of a certain unit, the Main Staff, or the HVO HZ-HB, so that this wouldn't continue in the future, and then there were three paragraphs in this order. Would you care to comment?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. There were individuals who, out of ignorance or because of malevolence, they issued statements to the public sometimes revealing military secrets, shouldn't be too amazed because we are a voluntary force -- volunteer force, and this is why the Main Staff issued such an order, whereby everybody was prohibited from issuing statements to the public. And the second, when journalists under item 2, with authorisation to work, visit the operational zone headquarters or formations, they must send to the komandant who is going to choose the individual, who is going to follow them while they are within the zone of responsibility, and it is best that somebody from the IPD sector does this. And this was our standard operating procedure which was respected. Later on, IPD personnel were in charge of receiving journalists. And under item 3, press conferences are the responsibility of the Defence Department, IPD sector, and all others within the zone's headquarters and information can organise. Conferences are based "upon my permission," as it states here, and this is how things happened particularly in the operation zone of Central Bosnia, with which we did not maintain communication because of the fact that they were encircled by the enemy and they had to make due on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you stated under item 2, you stated this was generally done in this manner, when you say "IPD," would it be the IPD of your sector or IPD personnel from the units?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: IPD personnel from the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next document, which is P 856. This is another order of the chief of the Main Staff concerning tasks, under 1, to commanders and assistants for information and propaganda. This is still the 4th of December 1992. Could you please explain to the Chamber what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Because of instances of improper conduct, Mr. Petkovic, chief of the Main Staff, issued this order whereby he tasks all commanders and assistants for information and propaganda to work more with the men, explain to them the possible tragic consequences of such conduct by individuals or groups. This is a pre-Christmas period. People tend to get more relaxed. More drink more alcoholic beverages, walk around armed, which means that there is a possibility for events with tragic consequences, and this is why the commander issued such a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, P 2331, is in your binder. Please take a look at it. This is a letter by Mr. Milivoj Petkovic, chief of the Main Staff, to the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Bruno Stojic, dated 12th of May, 1993, and it says here: "Pursuant to the request from operation zone and brigade levels in the HZ-HB for information on events in the HZ-HB," et cetera, and then there's this order. Could you please explain what this is about?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: This request means better engagement and better information dissemination among military units on all events in the territory of the HZ-HB. I understand this request to be a need that was perceived by Mr. Petkovic for better information to be disseminated, and this is what he requests from Mr. Stojic, head of the Defence Department, that he use IPD channels to improve information dissemination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to our instructions to highlight problems with interpretation, I must highlight that in English, this document was erroneously translated. This is a request, in Croatian, but it has been translated as an order. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. My learned colleague is right. I see in the original that this is a request, rather than an order. This translation, well, it's irrelevant. It's a P document, so it's within the realm of the Prosecution. I'm sorry I did not notice this before.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, this would be internal information dissemination, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, which is 2D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, since I remember things well, I can see that Mr. Petkovic's document is dated the 12th of May, i.e., three days after those events that occurred in Mostar. If we had enough time, we could show the video in which one can see soldiers who had captured Muslim soldiers. Clearly, this was circulated in the media. This operation was specifically targeted by the media. Had it been authorised or not, I don't know. As far as you are concerned, when a unit shows, on television, how a military operation was conducted, does this mean that this can only be shown with prior approval from the Department or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, yes. But in this specific case the service did not give the green light, and if it had been able to, it would have prevented POWs from being shown on video. You can't show POWs in the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, Judge Antonetti asked you about a certain event, and I'm going to ask you whether you had any authorisation or possibility -- well, if television stations that came in, did you have the authority to give the go-ahead or not if they didn't contact you? Did you have any authorisation?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Well, we could accredit them. That was the rule. They would report to us and we would accredit them. But some television crews and journalists came in with UNPROFOR, for example, others with humanitarian organisations, and others were taken 'round by various people and went about their business without our knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, we're going to discuss a very interesting subject, the accreditation given by you to journalists that went to Heliodrom, but I'm asking you specifically with respect to the question just asked you by Judge Antonetti. Did you -- were you in any way able to make a selection or decide what they would show and tag, film or not? And if you gave your authorisation, were you able to influence them and did you have any influence on what they would show or not on the material they obtained?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I've already said that we didn't censor anything, nor did we have the technical abilities of doing that, nor was that our intention, but at the very beginning we could point out to them what the problem was and reach an agreement, perhaps, with the journalists to see what they were interested in and give them the possibility of seeing what they wanted to see, talk to people, film what they wanted, fully conscious of the fact that every time that material could be put to bad use. But we took on this risk consciously and knew that somebody might make a montage of something or depict the situation which did not correspond to reality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, and I'm talking about the way that information was disseminated to the public, so let's look at 2D 00367 now, please. This is an order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, your answer is an interesting one. You said there was never any censorship. Is it because you had decided to be totally transparent or because of lack of competence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was a decision that was made at a far higher level than my level, because if the responsible had decided to implement censorship, they would have found somebody other than me, and they thought that nothing should be hidden. And proof of that is that I issued over 2.000 permissions and authorisations to foreign journalists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, as far as I remember, since I don't have the video here today -- if we were working the way I would wish to work, I would just press on a button and we would be able to see the clip. A video was shot on Muslims who are taken to the stadium in Mostar. This video, I believe, was circulated by the Spanish media. The foreign press -- the foreign media was there at the time. Did you know they were there at the time, that they were filming, or was this something that was totally beyond your control?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that particular case passed without my knowledge. I investigated the matter, and I received information, which was never actually confirmed, that the footing was -- footage was made by some soldiers from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you know that UNPROFOR soldiers had cameras and that they were filming everything they saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I assumed that they had cameras.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the next document, just briefly, and we're still on the subject of the flow of information, it is 2D 637. Have you found it? Yes, it's on e-court. We have here an order dated the 20th of September, 1993, when it's -- and it says: "In order to inform the public objectively, I command all the information for the media about the situation on the battle-field will be exclusively approved by a public relations officer from the HVO main headquarters." My first question is whether such a person existed, whether such a person was appointed to that kind of post? And, secondly, was everybody in the HVO HZ-HB satisfied, were they all satisfied with the way information was distributed, disseminated, how you received information, how you put information out and so on? So was this an example of an attempted intervention, or generally may we have your comments?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I was conscious of the fact that not everybody was satisfied with my work. Some people told me that; others, of course, did not. I cannot say for sure -- well, I see the contents and know the contents of this order, but I can't say -- well, up until this time, I can say that there wasn't a man for IPD in the Main Staff. After this, possibly. So as I can say -- as I say, there was a reconstruction of the Main Staff, a new organisation set up, and soon afterwards the Defence Department underwent change and a political administration was set up subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What you're talking about now, is that the period after Mr. Stojic ceased to be head of the Defence Department, when you're talking about this political administration?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, this document -- well, Mr. Vegar, you should have received this document, and did you?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just one more detail to clear up. You said that you don't know whether any IPD man existed in the Main Staff, and when you say that, you use the term -- you equate that with spokesman. You seem to use it the same way?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, the IPD person is usually the spokesman.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Now we'll go through the next documents fairly quickly. Look at 2D 00656, the next document, which is a programme of work, a work programme for moral guidance for 1992, and it contains the dynamics of all that. It was compiled on the 19th of October, 1992. It was signed by Mr. Bozo Rajic, and we have here certain appraisals made to which -- it says the sector for moral guidance, or rather the IPD, is a relatively recent date in comparison to some other functions and sectors in the Department of Defence. And it says the awareness of the need to establish this sector and of its complex functions has had difficulties getting through and getting proper treatment. Now, can you just briefly comment on that? Although this was written by Mr. Rajic, I assume that you were in the sector at the time, so can you comment on that first sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Generally speaking in the HVO, as a volunteer organisation, people were not trained and educated to take up the post of commanders and so on, so they themselves were not able to comprehend the importance of a service of this kind within the army, and some commanders put up resistance to the service. And I think that Mr. Rajic had that in mind when writing this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the second paragraph of this document, where it says: "In order to create efficient and well-thought-out system in this important area of work, it will be necessary to make maximum efforts and invest knowledge and work in connecting fragmented and varying information and propaganda structures and to establish the necessary chain of vertical and horizontal links and introduce responsibility and efficiency." Now, what vertical and horizontal links does this refer to? Because later, with this work programme and horizontal and vertical links, well, they were mentioned subsequently, in subsequent documents, so let's clear that up straight away.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I understand this in the following way: There were people in IPD, but not at all positions, so all the planned positions had to be replenished in the operative zones and so on, they had to be filled, and firm links be established between them and among them, and responsibility, too, and then between them and the commander, and especially coordination -- well, to build up coordination -- where it says "vertical links," that is at the level of a brigade, for example; I mean, horizontal, at the level of a brigade or the same level. But when we say "vertical," then down the professional chain. If we're dealing with the military psychologists, then a higher-level military psychologist, down to the Administration for Military Psychology, and the same applies for all the other instances.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, these links, were they supposed to exist with the sector of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So these links were supposed to exist, as we said, horizontally and vertically with the sector of the Defence Department for gathering and sending out information?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at the next document, 2D 00677 is the number, and it is a document which represents a report -- a work report following on from the work programme. So if we look at paragraph 2 there and look at the last sentence in that paragraph - that's the one I'd like to focus on - the inward flow of information is very poor, most frequently nonexistent, and the transmission and provision of information to military units has been of local significance only. The norm has been the absence of unity and obligation. Every locality has operated autonomously and independently of a single goal. Now, when I asked you whether there was the norm or obligation for you to receive all information, is that what this paragraph addresses? And what does it say when it says "exclusively local importance"? Can you comment upon that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Well, I didn't write this report, but I can comment, and these would be my comments: It's clear that the service didn't function as well as it could have because it had just been set up, just been in existence for a few months, so logically there would be problems. And when the local character is mentioned, then I think that means that Mr. Rajic, who wrote this report, had in mind local links between commanders and their assistance to the local environment, because we should know that just before the establishment of the Defence Department and the establishment of the HVO, there were municipal units and municipal staffs that were superior to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, when we come to reports, Mr. Vegar, while you worked in the field, did you compile reports, send them out to the Defence Department, and were those reports of yours parts of the HVO HZ-HB reports? And I'm speaking about annual and six-monthly reports?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at the work for 1992. P 00128 is the number, and I'd like to ask you to look at page 15 of that report. It is 15 in both the Croatian and English versions. Paragraph 3 on page 15, which speaks about the work of the IPD, and the first paragraph addresses what I asked you a moment ago, and that's why I said that it was a draft report. Now, you've seen this report, so can you confirm that everything that is contained in the report is roughly what happened in 1992, in the three months that you were working in the IPD in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at the next document, P 04699, which is a report on work for the period of June 1993; page 27 of the Croatian and page 18 of the English. And, Mr. Vegar, the same title appears here "Moral Guidance" or "Moral Upbringing," so we have the use of the IPD sector and the moral guidance sector, although that's the same sector, but you -- as you yourself said, these were different names for the same thing, the same sector. Now, Mr. Vegar, look at page 28, please, which refers to meetings with the IPD staff in the Military District of Western Herzegovina, and then it mentions seminars, the History Administration, the results achieved in sports, and so on. Now, tell me, were these meetings held from September 1992 with individual workers in the different operative zones in the different brigades?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, there were meetings in the operative zones and also individually in the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: These were professional meetings, as you said, where you would issue instructions on how work was to be done, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Specifically, I would like to know more, whether you conducted education on the application of international law and how you, within the framework of that sector at such meetings and seminars, how you conducted such education.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, this was one of our tasks. On several occasions, not once, we organised meetings and seminars with the help of representatives of the International Red Cross and with the help and on the basis of materials that we received from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, such brochures and leaflets on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Let's take a look at the last document in your binder. That's P 7419. Let's take a look at it. It is a report for the second six months of 1993. Please take a look at page 13, concerning the moral guidance sector. I'll quote what I'm interested in. You say here that the sector worked insensibly, particularly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Would you be so kind and give the page of the English version also?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is my problem. I will rectify that. I have only the Croatian version in front of me. But the page starts with "The moral guidance sector," with those words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It is page 4, then, page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, the sentence starts: "The sector was intensively working on information and propaganda by way of numerous press conferences through talks with more than 2.000 foreign journalists. This is the number of press IDs that were issued by the reception/guidance escort to the front-lines, and other locations that are attractive for the media." Please, let's analyse this. You answered about that as by His Honour Antonetti, on the number of foreign journalists. What does this mean, "the reception, guidance, direction and escort to the front-lines"? Could we break this down a bit, how this went? Would they address you or come to you? What did you do after such requests were lodged?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: When I would receive a request by a media crew, I tried to address it to the best of my abilities. Of course, journalists are interested in what their editors and their public are interested in, and there were requests to go to the front-line, to the forward positions. They were interested in visiting hospitals, prisons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If they wanted to go to the forward positions on the front-line, how would you issue them with accreditations? Would you go with them? Who would escort them? How was this done?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Of course, I had to be mindful of their security, and for that reason, at least one soldier would escort them. He would take a route which would not endanger their lives, but only to the spot where journalists demanded, but not beyond that point, to avoid threat to life, so that they could have footage and statements from people on the ground and not just my statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who would be in charge of them at certain unit level?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Well, they would come to a military unit. IPD personnel were supposed to meet them there and be there at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What kind of IPD, Mr. Vegar?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That unit's IPD personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you escort media to prisons in the territory of HZ-HB? Did you issue accreditations to media crews and whether you escorted them there? For instance, how many accreditations you issued in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I think that I handed out several to visit the military investigation prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Which military investigation prison?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: The Mostar military investigation prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was that the Heliodrom locality prison?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you recall in which period this took place?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That was July/August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, would you escort them on occasion?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: At least once, I escorted a team of journalists.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you escort representatives of the International Red Cross when they visited the Heliodrom military investigation prison?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you visited the prison with journalists, who did you seek approval from and what were the technical arrangements to visit the Heliodrom prison?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I would seek approval from the commander of the prison, Stanko -- I can't remember the family name.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please try harder. Maybe it will come back to you later. You contacted him. What did you say to him? I think this is an important question, so please make your answer very precise. You called him?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I called him and told him that there is a team of journalists who would like to visit the prison. If it was possible, we could come. He said it was possible, and then I would write an approval for the departure of those journalists towards the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would it be the same procedure every time they asked that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Every time they asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On that one occasion that you escorted journalists to that location, that was also in July/August 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Who met you there, what did you see there, and what the journalist did, who they talked to? Did they produce footage, take pictures?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: We were met by the commander of the prison. He talked to the journalists. They visited a room containing prisoners. They went to the toilet, a kitchen. They visited -- well, a doctor met us in a room, and a nurse, a male nurse. Journalists talked with prison ers. They taped that conversation. There was a photojournalist, so she took pictures. We were there maybe 45, 50 minutes in all.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you were there with representatives of the International Red Cross, can you recall whether this was before the visit to -- with the journalists or what was the sequence of those visits?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I visited the prison with the ICRC personnel first.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you recall who requested that you escort them to the military investigation prison?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I can't recall anybody calling me, but since I cooperated with the International Red Cross, I asked the chief warden to approve a visit and then we visited.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: How long did this visit with the ICRC take? Did you see the same locations?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. It lasted no longer than an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, during your two visits -- at least two visits to the prison, did you see any women, children, being detained there?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: No, I did not see any women or children, although I must admit that in town later on, I heard that there were several women with children in the loft. Maybe several days afterwards, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm asking you about what you heard. Did you hear about the reasons for them being there?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I heard that they were refugees, that they had nowhere else to go, that some of them didn't want to leave the prison, and this is the only information that I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you hear such information from official persons, since you are a person who received information through vertical and horizontal channels, so did you hear this about women and children through official sources?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: No. It was unofficial.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did journalists request that -- to visit Dretelj and Gabela prisons? Were there any requests? Did you know about those prisons? Were you asked to issue approvals?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: There were such requests, but I couldn't issue any approvals for such prisons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, did you know who was in charge of those prisons, and did you send journalists to those persons who were in those of those prisons?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Tomo Sakota was in charge of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you send the journalists to him? Did you know who appointed Mr. Sakota to take charge of those prisons?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I knew that he was appointed by Mr. Mate Boban, and since I could not satisfy such requests, I would send journalists to him. And if he were to allow them, then that was it, but I couldn't do anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We are revisiting the topics of your meetings, Mr. Vegar. We'll have to speed up. Let's take a look at document 2D 665.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, may I refer to the last document. You may be able to answer or maybe not. It is my feeling that this document P 70919 as -- comes from the Defence Department and is about activities from July to December 1993, and now I see something which is stated here, and I should like you to give me your opinion on this if you have one, of course, if not, then just tell me that you cannot answer. It says that the armed forces from the HR HB [as interpreted] have become professional brigades through the abolition of the professional brigades, and the most interesting comes afterwards. The latter were not reporting to the Staff of the HV. Now, can you explain this to me -- well, there's a mistake. I'm saying once again to the interpreters in English to pay attention carefully. I said "HVO." I did not say "HV." I hate to have to control what I'm saying. You know, when I say something, I would like this to be transcribed faithfully. So, sir, about these professional units, have you heard from them? Have you heard about them or not? If you have not heard about them, then I will stop my questions there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't find that passage in the text. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the text, this is on the first page, second paragraph. The first page starts for the period from July to December, and this is the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can assist you, that's page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it. But since this did not concern directly my sector, I did not read this passage. I would need some time to read this passage. And, anyway, I did not understand the question fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I assist? You expect a witness's answer. He states that he didn't read that part of the text and he didn't understand fully the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, sir, you know, don't look at the document. All I'm saying is that this document refers to professional units which were not reporting to the headquarters of the HVO. So what do you think about that? Do you know, don't you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know of any such units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, you don't. We'll ask Mr. Praljak the question when he testifies, or to other witnesses, military witnesses. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, please take the next binder, the new binder. The first document is 2D 00655. Please take a look at it, please. This is a report from working meetings at brigade level in the Operation Zone South-East Herzegovina, organised with the cooperation of the moral guidance sector of the Defence Department, and the Operation Zone South-East Herzegovina. You remember those meetings? There is -- this document bears your signature, testifying that you attended those meetings. At the beginning it's said that there was one meeting in 1993. One was on the 6th of January, the 9th of January, the 11th of January, and the 14th of January. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber who -- what was this meeting on the 14th of January with the 1st Mostar Brigade? That's one that was part later of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. Even after that date, we had joint meetings with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, was -- were those meetings with IPD personnel of those brigades?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At such meetings, you discussed different problems and topics, and this is a report from such a meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go through some other reports. Please take a look at the next document, 2D 00635. This is a report on negotiations on the exchange of military and civilian prisoners in the Konjic municipality. It's dated the 31st of May, 1993. It is evident from this document that a commission was established by Mr. Petkovic which was supposed to conduct an exchange of military and civilian prisoners captured in the municipality of Konjic, pursuant to an agreement by Generals Petkovic and Halilovic, dated the 12th of May. It is stated here who was in that commission, and a name Vera Cubela was quoted here. She worked in your sector?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. She was a psychologist in my sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Was it important for the morale of your units -- it was important not only to exchange prisoners of war but also to exchange the bodies of killed soldiers and civilians; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's very important for any military organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you asked, at such meetings, why this was important? Did you receive requests from units? Was it -- were you requested to explain what happened, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes. For every combatant, it was important to know whether their -- when they were to be exchanged or freed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would people ask about the fate of their beloved ones, members of their families, of course, whether they were killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, these were even more important questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, could you tell us whether this exchange did take place and what happened, pursuant to information that you must have received from your colleague, Vera Cubela, who worked under you at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the agreement between Mr. Petkovic and Halilovic was -- did not take place. Our group of officers went to the municipality of Konjic, but the exchange of military and civilian prisoners did not take place, and the people from the BiH Army were to blame. They were not ready to fulfill the items of this agreement, the agreement of two generals, one of whom was their superior officer. There were two commissions that were supposed to work on resolving these issues, but it was obviously a ploy to procrastinate, and those people returned from Konjic with the task unfulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I now want to show you some documents which directly relate to what you were talking about, the information that you received directly or through the media which relate to the situation in the field, on the ground, and that was information that you received and that you used to inform the public at large, and others that you used for internal information. So in that respect, look at 2D 00682, and this is a piece of information which came from Prozor, from the Operative Zone of South-West Herzegovina, and it says the GH HVO Mostar, IPD department. And you said that in the Main Staff, there was no IPD department, at least not at that time, so tell us briefly whether you can remember why this kind of information was supposed to go to the IPD, which means the IPD sector and to you; right?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I think that motivation was as follows, the motivation of the author of this piece of information, and that is that from the IPD, somebody should help find a journalist, a television crew, to record the events in Prozor and the release of BH POWs taken during the previous conflicts, and the object being to reduce tension and as a confidence-building measure. So the commander was of the opinion that if this would be broadcast over television, it would boost confidence between the two peoples living in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says: "Calm intentions between the HVO and --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, we're going to take a break now. It's 20 to. We're going to take a 20-minute break, and we'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have been told that I have roughly an hour left, which means that we'll go on until the end of the day today and end there, if there are no major interruptions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, I've been asked by the French interpreters that we slow down, speak a little more slowly. So I'll do my best, and you do your best, too, and especially to pause between my questions and your answers. And before we go on to the next document, I'd like to correct the transcript. On page 68, line 5, a document is lacking there that I showed the witness, and that was document P 00128. It was an HVO HZ-HB report for 1992. Now, Mr. Vegar, you told us the way in which things influenced morale or, rather, news of deaths, woundings, and people having been taken prisoner all influenced morale. Now I'd like to ask you to look at the next document, which is 2D 00815, and tell me whether you've found it.

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a report by the assistant command of the brigade for ID [as interpreted], the Herceg Stjepan Brigade from Konjic, and it was sent to the HVO, the Main Staff, the Command of the Operative Zone, Mr. Zebic, and it addresses the situation in Trusina. Can you tell us, please, whether you know or whether you received information about what happened. And we see that this is the 16th and the 17th of April, the stamp received by the Main Staff. Can you tell the Court whether you received any information about what was going on in Trusina specifically at that time, and could you tell me how that information influenced morale in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. This goes to what we addressed earlier today, and I think before counsel -- before the question is answered, counsel should comply with the Chamber's ruling and indicate why this particular evidence is elicited and how it relates to something other than tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I acted upon your instructions, because I asked the witness in advance, before I ever showed him any document, what the -- how different situations influenced morale, that is to say, information about HVO members being taken prisoner, or killed, or possibly civilian casualties, fatalities. I didn't say that they were war crimes or anything else. And the witness answered that this did indeed have a considerable effect on morale among the HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, first and foremost, you should ask the person in question whether he was aware of it, because he may never have been aware of it. When I see that the document was sent to the Main Staff of the HVO and to the commander of the operational zone in the south-east, perhaps the witness was never made aware of this document. Maybe this is of no interest whatsoever. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, in addition to that, Your Honour, to say that it's relevant to showing how it affected morale doesn't answer the question. How is that relevant to this case? How is the morale of these soldiers relevant to any issue in the case? So that doesn't answer the question. What is the purpose of this evidence as it relates to a relevant issue in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, try and tell us what the connection is with the indictment. If there is a connection, then you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in this document, in the third line, it says: "Some of our soldiers are in a serious psychological condition because their families are imprisoned in that village." Now, we have here someone who was in charge, among other things, of morale, the morale of the soldiers, and therefore quite simply I consider that he could tell us something about that. Now, whether he knew of this document or of these events I consider to be very important as an indicator of what was happening during that time in the area, and I think it's impossible to answer the charges of a joint criminal enterprise if we cannot address the events that influenced morale, and the witness is best placed to answer that question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, I think that there is perhaps a misunderstanding. The question was not whether and how this influenced on the morale. The question was: What is the relevance of the morale of HVO soldiers with regard to the indictment? And that is not quite obvious. No, the question was really to Ms. Nozica. I don't know why you often pop up and answer questions put to someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because that's what lawyers do, Your Honour. When they are trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Karnavas, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what lawyers do -- well, I mean, we seem to be getting off the wrong foot. I'm entitled to make a record, and if I do feel the need to make a point, I will make a point. And if you wish to sanction me, then sanction me. Give me a hearing, and we can proceed. Now, it does go to the issue of reverse ethnic cleansing. That's why. And that's my contribution to the Bench. If we're here to get to the truth and you're asking why, it does relate to reverse ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, I still think that when a Defence calls a witness, it's for that Defence to say what it wants to establish with that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stood up. You could have easily told me to sit down and shut up, as you did to one of our witnesses. You could do that, have you that right. But I also have the right to make a record and make a contribution, and in my opinion the joint criminal enterprise affects everyone, everyone in this case, including my client, and that's why I'm entitled to make the record. This is an international tribunal, and these are the rules. I play by the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to hear Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, don't add to the tension, please. Let Ms. Nozica answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree with what my learned friend Mr. Karnavas just said, and I would like to thank him for that, and I said the broader context, without entering into the specificities, which is certainly part of the joint criminal enterprise, but the broader context is that this relates to the joint criminal enterprise, and the morale of soldiers is a very important element, if we look at everything that happened in HZ-HB. And, Judge Antonetti, you yourself said we don't know if the witness saw this or knew anything about this information, but I don't think we should consider these matters in front of the witness. We can ask the witness whether he knows about any of this, and then we can hear his answer to see whether these events influenced the morale of the soldiers, and then it will be up to the Trial Chamber to weigh up whether this is relevant or not. Now, Your Honour Judge Trechsel, I could respond very precisely and tell you what all these events in April relate to, April 1993, including this particular event, because it testifies to certain action undertaken by the BH Army which is exceptionally relevant, but I find myself in a position whereby I would be testifying here. So I kindly ask you to look at the documents. You will be able to weigh them up and assess their probative value, but I think that it is very important precisely because of the joint criminal enterprise and, as my colleague said a moment ago, Mr. Karnavas, because of reverse ethnic cleansing, what was happening to these people, precisely because of the indictment which relates to Sovici, and I think that it is exceptionally important for us to establish what was going on in this area, what the casualties and fatalities were among the Croatian civilians from the BH Army, and then, of course, members of the HVO as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I quite respect my colleagues. The answer simply -- the question simply hasn't been answered. The Chamber's ruling requires -- counsel says she's afraid of testifying. The Chamber's ruling requires that she articulate a basis, and if that requires her to say -- to give a basis, then so be it. If we need to excuse the witness, you know, we can do that. But there is simply -- with great respect to those in the courtroom, there has still been no answer to the question. To say that a reversed -- reverse ethnic cleansing doesn't make any obvious connection, and to say that it relates to morale doesn't tell us how it relates to the indictment. And I want to be very clear. I'm not trying to be obstinate for obstinate's sake, but this is the point of this evidence, and the reason we filed a motion was to put it before the Chamber, because I don't think it's going to be the last time that it happens, and that's where -- that's what this is about. And counsel has to articulate a specific reason why this is relevant to something put in issue by the indictment, and with great respect it hasn't been done yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, as far as I'm concerned, as far as I'm concerned, I see that it is your belief that this relates to joint criminal enterprise, and I fear that, while the situation is a bit ambivalent, to take now a negative decision as far as your request is concerned would not be very safe, so I, for myself, declare myself satisfied with your explanation, which does not mean that I am convinced by it, in substance, but as far as this phase of the proceedings is concerned, for me you could go along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Very precisely, I'd like the witness -- well, the witness is a means -- a vehicle through which we're going to establish facts in respect of the joint criminal enterprise, so let me ask him straight away.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, did you know anything about these events, and did you receive direct information about the events in Trusina, and otherwise in this area during April, what kind of information did you receive, which information did you receive? Just answer precise -- answer my question precisely. And how did that affect the morale of the soldiers or, rather, did it require you to establish certain matters, and did you ask anybody to do that?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I am well aware of the events in Trusina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that there is a lot of noise and interference in the courtroom, and we're not able to hear the speakers, so could the other microphones be switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... on the right banks of the Neretva River, in the area of what is called the Neretvica. And as the author of this piece of information states himself, that is where some very ugly and tragic things took part -- took place. And we see that on the 17th of April, to the best of my recollections -- on the 16th the slaughter took place in the place called Trusina, so he just has indications that the situation is very difficult there, serious, but he didn't have any detailed information as to what had actually happened. So in this piece of information, he is asking for the assistance of the Red Cross and asking the Red Cross to come in.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, later on did you receive information about the -- or through the IPD? Did you inform the public in HZ-HB that this crime had been committed and who the fatalities were?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: This piece of information did come in, and it was accessible to the public. Later on, we learnt the names of the people who were killed in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let us look at document 2D 00157, page 1 of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to address the issue of morale. I'm trying to understand what could have happened in Hamici [phoen]. What date is Hamici, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think on the 16th or 17th of April, at the same time or slightly later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's later, any information on Trusina could have had an impact on those people that may have committed crimes in Hamici or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it could have, but whether it did or not, I don't know, because I did not have such information, neither did I have an assessment of the situation in Central Bosnia. As I already stated, we had -- they were isolated, in terms of communication, for a long time, and I don't believe that these two events were connected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document we have before us, is this a document you were made aware of or not? Not this one, but the previous document, the document about Trusina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was informed of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How did you get to know about it, since it had been sent to the Main Staff of the HVO? You were not one of the recipients of this document. How did you get it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I already stated, Your Honour, the Main Staff is probably the main source of information that I received. Somebody from the Main Staff most probably gave it to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gave it to you. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The document 2D 00157, have you found it? It is signed by Mr. Darinko Tadic, lists the names of people who perished in war crimes against the Croats in the municipality of Konjic. Did you receive information about those people being casualties?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: I have some information dating before this date, but we found and learned about the names and family names afterwards, not then.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please take a look at page 2. This is a list of villages in the municipality of Konjic populated by Croats. Some were burnt down, looted, and the Croats were expelled, it says here. Please take a look at item 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I have had so far no intention to discuss this matter again, and I also agreed to have a few questions concerning this issue. On the other hand, I would like again to emphasise that the argument which was raised by you, Ms. Nozica, and also by Mr. Karnavas, that is, the adverse and the reverse -- I'm sorry, the reverse ethnic cleansing, I do not think that it is really a solid and forceful argument in this case. I tell you why. That rule which I quoted at the beginning of this meeting, Rule 140 of the General Rules of Customary International Humanitarian Law, says, and I again repeat: "The obligation to respect and ensure respect for International Humanitarian Law does not depend on reciprocity," does not depend on reciprocity. And here again it is my point that although we all know about those very regretful and criminal acts, and we on all sides of this whole, we do condemn them, at the same time somehow I do not understand the relationship between the morale of the troops, if these criminal acts have been committed here and there, and committed of course on the other side, at least crimes which were originally committed in other, of course, instances by other troops, so that's why I really feel that if you are now to continue with this way of thinking, then again we are going against the general rule of the Customary International Law, that the obligation of respect of the rules do not -- does not depend on reciprocity. And therefore, in my view, they cannot be overestimated, even if, regretfully, we all admit that there were certain very important breaches of International Humanitarian Law everywhere and originally by everyone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in my opinion, and this is why I'm asking to say a few words, this problem is concerning the most important bit of the whole proceedings. Of course, no crime can be justified by another crime, and of course no commander should allow or issue an order to answer to a crime by a crime, but we're dealing with psychology of people. We're talking about decompensating persons, not morale. We talk about a number of decompensated people. We're talking about the power to control non-structured units which are in the grip of hatred. And a commander can be assessed or evaluated on their powers to do something in May 1993 in Mostar. 115 people were slaughtered on the left bank. All of them had relatives, and the number of decompensated persons who are ready for revenge is something that a commander or a civilian official is confronted with in that town, and to manage such a crowd, within civil authority or state authority organs, is what we're dealing with. We are not justifying crime by crime. We're not talking about Praljak issuing an order to answer by crime to a crime. But if we list the crimes in Grabovica and elsewhere, then the number of decompensated persons in a volunteer force -- armed force, the question for Praljak, Stojic, or anybody is how to prevent. How can we prevent what happened in Greece, in France, the balijas [as interpreted], about the events in Iraq? This is the merits of these whole proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have information about propaganda and information. I'm going to address another issue. I see that this is sent by Mr. Tadic to the ICRC, the Red Cross, UN observers and UNPROFOR. This document gives a list of all those communities in which Croats fell. This is my question, Witness: When something happens like happened in Ahmici, the international community was mobilised, whereas -- well, when it is informed about all of this, was there such a mobilisation? And if nothing happened, can you give us an explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, your question would require broader analysis, an explanation. It is true that the international community was informed of the crimes that we see referred to in Mr. Tadic's document. I can frankly relay the feelings of those people in Herzegovina and elsewhere, that asked themselves the very same question that you are asking, why crimes committed by one side is taken by the international community and UNPROFOR in one way and a completely different radical vengeful way to the crimes committed by the other side. I do not have an answer to your question. I still do not have a definitive opinion or stance on this issue, not only concerning the events in 1992/1993, but also the present conduct of some international representatives in that area even today.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, I would like to ask you to comment under item 18 of this document in front of you. It says here: "The Croats from the town of Konjic were either expelled or detained in Celebic (about 300 persons in the camp)." Mr. Vegar, we saw the minutes of that meeting on an exchange of civilians and HVO members that were present and captured in that area after these events. Do you recall -- can you confirm that this concerned the persons referred to here?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under 19: "The villages of Turija, Zabrdje and Zaslivlje, the fate of the Croat residents of these villages is unknown. The village is now populated by the Croat refugees from the town of Konjic." Mr. Vegar, at time before this date in March or April, did you have any information that Croats, members of HVO and civilians had been expelled to those three villages?

utterances.speaker: VESO VEGAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did have information. Quite a lot of Croats from Konjic were expelled, and they stayed there for a long time, some even until the very end of the war, because these three villages remained in their control.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Vegar, there is a host of questions I'd like to ask you about, very important questions. Pleases skip the next document, for time's sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm doing what you would have liked to do, Ms. Nozica. I find this document really important and relevant, and my hesitations were not global. Mr. Vegar, can you vouch or say that everything on this list, number 1 to 23, is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With a high degree of being sure that I can vouch, say that these information are correct, but whether there were 300 or 290, 250, or 350 people detained at Celebici, this I cannot say.
